newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bertelsmann sees EU clearing pay TV deal.
newsitem.headline: Bertelsmann sees EU clearing pay TV deal.

text.p: Bertelsmann AG chief executive Michael Dornemann was quoted on Saturday as saying he did not expect the European Union to block a plan by Bertelsmann and the Kirch group to become equal partners in pay TV broadcaster Premiere.
Dornemann was quoted in an interview with Focus magazine as saying he and Leo Kirch had spoken to European Union Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert about the cooperation plan.
"The conversation went well. I don't expect any problems," Dornemann was quoted as saying.
Focus released the interview on Saturday ahead of publication in Monday's editions.
The plan to combine the pay-TV channels Premiere and Kirch's DF1 digital broadcaster did not give Bertelsmann and Kirch a dominant market position, Dornemann said.

He added that a stock market flotation of affiliated channel RTL was not on the agenda at present but added it would be an interesting possibility in the medium term, as last Monday's flotation of private broadcaster ProSieben had shown.
RTL belongs to the CLT-Ufa group whose major shareholders are Bertelsmann and Luxembourg's Audiofina.
